purpose: Reference check of the CDM 3.0.3 relation-triple layer, as frozen and as cleaned by DeepSeek (outputs/results/cleaned_layer_deepseek), against BugSigDB (human-curated microbial signatures) and CTD (curated chemical-disease and gene-disease associations). Rules fixed before the run; this file's sha256 is written to PREREGISTRATION.sha256 before any result is computed.
triples: all 25,788 rows of the CDM relation table; entity types from canonical_term.cdm_type of subject_term_id / object_term_id

identifier_resolution.rule: an entity is resolved by (1) its CDM mapping, else (2) an exact, case-insensitive name match in the reference vocabulary; a name matching more than one identifier is unresolved. The method used is recorded per item.
identifier_resolution.cdm_mapping_rows: term_concept_map rows with mapping_disposition_reviewed = 'ACCEPTED', or is_canonical_candidate = 1 with mapping_disposition != 'REJECTED' and mapping_disposition_reviewed not in ('REJECTED', 'REMOVED')
identifier_resolution.taxon: NCBITaxon IDs from mapping rows; names.dmp names of any class
identifier_resolution.chemical: MeSH IDs from mapping rows (bioportal MESH URIs, mesh service IDs); CTD_chemicals name and synonyms
identifier_resolution.disease: MeSH IDs from mapping rows; CTD_diseases name and synonyms (CTD IDs MESH:* or OMIM:*)
identifier_resolution.gene: entity types PROTEIN, DNA_RNA, GENOMICS only: human gene_info symbol or synonym, upper-cased, at least 3 characters

bugsigdb_taxon.unit: (triple, paper) pairs for papers in both CDM and BugSigDB (matched by PMID, else DOI), triple with at least one ORGANISM side resolved to a taxon (the subject if both are organisms)
bugsigdb_taxon.verdicts: MATCH = taxon ID in a BugSigDB signature of that paper; PARTIAL = same genus (nodes.dmp lift); NOT_IN_REFERENCE otherwise
bugsigdb_taxon.chance: the same taxon scored against the BugSigDB taxa of every other overlap paper

bugsigdb_direction.unit: MATCH/PARTIAL pairs where the taxon is the subject and the relation is directional
bugsigdb_direction.rule: SAME / OPPOSITE when BugSigDB gives one direction for the matched taxa in that paper; else UNDETERMINED. Scored for the original relation and, for kept triples, for the cleaned relation (a swapped triple whose taxon moved to the object is UNDETERMINED).
bugsigdb_direction.chance: agreement expected from the up/down base rates of the determinable pairs

ctd_chemical_disease.unit: triples with one CHEMICAL side and one DISEASE side, both resolved
ctd_chemical_disease.verdicts: CURATED = pair with DirectEvidence in CTD; INFERRED_ONLY = pair present only as inferred; NOT_IN_REFERENCE
ctd_chemical_disease.chance: share of all cross pairs (distinct resolved chemicals x distinct resolved diseases of these triples) that are in CTD, curated and any

ctd_gene_disease.unit: triples with one gene-type side (resolved to a human GeneID) and one DISEASE side (resolved)
ctd_gene_disease.chance: share of all cross pairs (distinct genes x distinct diseases) in CTD

cleaning_effect: difference in support (MATCH+PARTIAL for BugSigDB; any CTD support) between kept and dropped triples, with a Newcombe hybrid-score 95% interval; and direction agreement of the original vs the cleaned relation on the same kept pairs
answer_template: one record per checked item in items.jsonl, validated against answer_template.schema.json
reporting_rules: Report support by a reference, not accuracy: absence from BugSigDB or CTD is NOT_IN_REFERENCE, never 'wrong'.
CTD support does not show that the paper made the claim; it shows that the association is known elsewhere.
Name-matched identifiers are reported separately from CDM-mapped ones.
